notes:
PASS is contract_checked on the fake backend only: no ROS 2 graph, rosbridge, Gazebo, multiplexer node, sensor or hardware was run, and driver.lock.json keeps reviewed_by null. Scope is one robot namespace of auna_control's cmd_vel_multiplexer: the namespaced toggle_cmd_vel_source (auna_msgs/srv/SetString), get_source_status (std_srvs/srv/Trigger) and cmd_vel/teleop (geometry_msgs/msg/TwistStamped) input. The absolute /trigger_emergency_stop and /get_estop_status services are deliberately not bound because every namespaced multiplexer creates those same absolute names, so a call is not robot-scoped; this is a deployment assumption, not an upstream fact. The stop is the namespaced source-OFF service: it is a software source change, not an independent hardware e-stop, and the acknowledgement is not sensed vehicle quiescence. The multiplexer caches the last message per source, so selecting a non-OFF source re-publishes that cached command; the MHS latch cannot stop unrelated ROS clients from changing the source. The input is speed plus steering angle because the shipped convert_yaw_to_steering_angle=false copies twist.angular.z to drive.steering_angle; with that parameter true the meaning would become a yaw rate. G4 remained warn with two G4.REF_VALUE warnings, and they are expected: the cited model.urdf lines state the positive maximum magnitudes (10.0 m/s and 0.6458 rad) as absolute bounds, so the symmetric negative bounds (-10.0 and -0.6458) are implied but not printed on the cited line; no line in the clone prints those negative values. The active model.urdf plugin permits 10.0 m/s while the shipped and unused race_car model-parameter file records 1.5 m/s; the driver uses the active plugin bound and the included example site overlay narrows speed to the shipped 1.5 m/s. NOT COVERED: live ROS endpoint resolution and remapping, the multiplexer's 20 Hz repeated-command timer, Gazebo physics and the ackermann drive plugin, odometry, scan, camera/image/depth observations, Nav2/CACC/wallfollowing control, world step/reset, multi-robot coordination, and any hardware or F1TENTH platform run. The fake is an analytic ROS-free F0 contract stand-in, not a replay of captured traffic; its placeholder state and command values are test data, and the plugin limits are recorded source facts. Install is empty: the operator supplies ROS 2 Humble, Gazebo and rosbridge.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked every endpoint and type, the SetString and Trigger definitions, all 17 facts, both limits, the fake and the stop against cmd_vel_multiplexer_node.cpp, topics.yaml, params.yaml, the launch files, docker-compose.yml, the race-car model and the teleop, control-panel and F1TENTH sources at the pin. The stop holds: toggle_cmd_vel_source OFF sets current_source_ before answering (308-337), the 20 Hz timer publishes zero on every output when the source is OFF, its only earlier branch is the e-stop flag, which also publishes zero, and input messages only update the per-source cache (359-417, 278-293). But the speed and steering limits were cited to model.urdf:395-417, which states only the positive absolute clamps 10.0 m/s and 0.6458 rad, and the author accepted the two UNSOURCED_LIMIT_GATE_WARNINGs; the status read had no success predicate; two facts claimed more than their lines (the params 'so' clause, initial_source passed on line 68); the docstring called /robot1 the default, although the launch defaults to robot0 and only docker-compose sets ROBOT_INDEX=1; and the competing teleop publisher, the control-panel client and the F1TENTH path were not disclosed. The reviewer made both limits operator_required, added the steering range to the example overlay, added the success predicate, corrected those facts and the docstring, added seven source facts, four gaps and a safe_state sentence (driver.py, site-limits.example.json), added envelope cases (test_driver.py), updated facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json. The gate and collect.py --strict pass with no warning; the digest changes to sha256:37aba6e6e1e94b39cd051f945e394f015bd87e196ae34eaa5fdc9f4d636f78ea, and the author's notes on the expected G4 warnings and on using the plugin bound are superseded. For the human reviewer: Simulated Ackermann race car (Gazebo). The e-stop selects source OFF on /robot1/toggle_cmd_vel_source; the multiplexer's wall timer then publishes zero speed and steering at 20 Hz and the plugin decelerates through its velocity PID; nothing senses the car stopping. Any toggle_cmd_vel_source client (the RViz control panel) can re-select a source, which re-publishes the cached command, while MHS is latched; the keyboard teleop of the docker-compose teleop and manual_control profiles publishes cmd_vel/teleop at 10 Hz. /robot1 matches the docker-compose deployment (ROBOT_INDEX=1); the bare launch default is robot0. The clone also ships an F1TENTH VESC platform launch: nothing connects the multiplexer to it, but a remap would make this package drive a real car, which needs a human hardware review.

catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class selects the input source of an upstream command multiplexer; the capability is a device-specific control-mode command over the namespaced toggle_cmd_vel_source service.

cap.motion.mobile_base.v1 requires a bounded duration and an angular velocity in rad/s, but the native multiplexer input is a speed plus a steering angle in rad: the shipped convert_yaw_to_steering_angle=false copies twist.angular.z directly to drive.steering_angle, so the class contract does not fit the native command or its one-message, timer-repeated semantics.
No catalogue read class covers the multiplexer's current command-source string; the upstream get_source_status Trigger callback only returns the stored source name.

cap.motion.stop.v1 takes a deceleration profile and reports a stopping position and stopped state, but the upstream stop only sets the velocity source to OFF and its acknowledgement provides no velocity, position or quiescence feedback; binding the class would overclaim a stop the source cannot prove.
